The clause «تعقلون» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of كنتم ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being فلا توالوهم (then do not take them as allies) or فلا تتّخذوا منهم أصدقاء (then do not take friends from among them).

* Morphology:
(بطانة), the close associates with whom a person shares his inner affairs; derived from البطن (belly) and الباطن (inner), as opposed to the outer. Its verb is of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعالة, with kasra on the fāʾ. It is a primitive (jāmid) noun, and it is a collective noun with no singular from its own root.
(خبالا), a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning corruption. Its origin is the disease and languor that afflicts an animal and brings about corruption or disorder in it. Its verb is خبل يخبل, of the class of ضرب. Without doubling, it is on the pattern فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ; or with doubling.
(البغضاء), a maṣdar like السرّاء and الضرّاء, from بغض يبغض, of the class of نصر, the class of كرم and the class of فرح; its pattern is فعلاء with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(أفواه), plural of فم. Its origin is فوه, so its lām (third radical) is a hāʾ; this is indicated by its plural being formed on that, and by its diminutive فويه. Its pattern is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn [Translator's note: thus in the source], and the pattern of أفواه is أفعال.
(صدور), plural of صدر, a primitive noun denoting a concrete entity; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- «لا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطانَةً» a man's biṭāna and walīja (confidant) is the one whom he lets know his secrets out of trust in him. It is likened to the lining (biṭāna) of a garment, just as it is likened to the undergarment (shiʿār). He ﷺ said: "The Anṣār are the undergarment (shiʿār) and the people are the outer garment (dithār)."
2- Infiṣāl (disengagement): it is that the speaker says something that gives the impression that it is something known and obvious, but it contains something beyond that, whose aim is further and whose reach is loftier. That is in His saying «مِنْ أَفْواهِهِمْ», for it is known that a person expresses what he conceals with his mouth; the infiṣāl in that is recording against them that they cannot restrain words from escaping their tongues that betray the feeling of hatred and rancour.
3- Ṭibāq (antithesis): between بدت and تخفي.

* Benefits:
His saying, the Exalted: «يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطانَةً مِنْ دُونِكُمْ».
1- We have already seen that «أي» is used as a means to address what is made definite by أل and the relative nouns, so أي becomes the one addressed, and the noun that follows it is parsed as a badal of it; the badal is permitted according to the form as it is permitted according to the position. As for the import of the verse, it is a warning against taking the Jews as allies, because of the evil and scheming they harboured against the believers. Perhaps this verse applies to the condition of the believers in every age, and they need to act by its content towards every sinful aggressor or intruding usurper. Few are those who act on the import of the speech of Allah and act according to what it requires.

safi-cedvel:73-73.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إلا) a particle of exception; (اللام) a preposition «[Note: The commentators and grammarians differed greatly over this verse, and more than nine ways were mentioned regarding it, but the clearest of them and the closest to the apparent meaning is what we indicated above.. Among these ways is that the lām in (لمن) is redundant (zāʾida), the verb تؤمنوا being made to carry the meaning of تصدقوا (believe/trust).. and the interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤتى..) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) whose governor is تؤمنوا.. etc.]», (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) of the implied (muqaddar) noun excepted from, with the preposition repeated; the implied form is: لا تؤمنوا لأحد إلّا لمن تبع دينكم (do not trust anyone except one who follows your religion) «[Note: The overall meaning of the verse then becomes, on the following implied form: لا تقرّوا ولا تعترفوا لأحد بأن يؤتى أحد مثل ما أوتيتم إلّا لمن تبع دينكم (do not acknowledge or admit to anyone that anyone is given the like of what you were given, except to one who follows your religion).]» (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الهدى) ism of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif; (هدى) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أن) a maṣdar particle that makes the verb subjunctive; (يؤتى) an imperfect verb, passive, subjunctive (manṣūb), the sign of the subjunctive being the fatḥa implied on the alif; (أحد) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (مثل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ما) a relative noun, mabnī, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (أوتيتم) a past verb, passive, mabnī on the sukūn.. and (تمّ) a pronoun, nāʾib fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يؤتى أحد) is in the position of genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e.: بأن يؤتى «[Note: al-ʿUkbarī made the interpreted maṣdar a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: لا تؤمنوا إلّا لمن تبع دينكم خشية أن يؤتي أحد ... (do not trust except one who follows your religion, for fear that anyone be given ...)]» and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تؤمنوا), the verb being made to carry the meaning of "acknowledge and admit" «[Note: It is also permissible for the interpreted maṣdar to be the khabar of (إنّ).. with هدى الله a badal of الهدى.. and (يحاجّوكم) subjunctive by an implied أن after أو in the sense of حتى.]», (أو) a conjunction; (يحاجّوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, conjoined to the verb يؤتى.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (يحاجّوكم); (ربّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قل) like the first; (إنّ الفضل) like إنّ الهدى; (بيد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of إنّ; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; (يؤتي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو; (من) a relative noun, mabnī, in the position of accusative as second mafʿūl bihi; (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is هو. (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (واسع) khabar, nominative; (عليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «لا تؤمنوا» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the request clause آمنوا — in the previous verse — because it is the completion of the speech of the group «[Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: among the commentators are those who held that this is from the speech of Allah, by which He makes firm the hearts of the believers lest they doubt at the forgery of the Jews.. And there is no disagreement and no doubt that His saying: «قل إنّ الهدى هدى الله» is from the speech of Allah.]».
The clause «تبع دينكم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «قل with what it governs» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «إنّ الهدى هدى الله» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of the saying).
The clause «يؤتى أحد» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «أوتيتم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «يحاجّوكم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يؤتى.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الفضل ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «يؤتيه» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of (إنّ).
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من). The clause «الله واسع» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Benefits:
1- The words of Allah the Exalted: «إِنَّ الْهُدى هُدَى اللَّهِ»: this clause is interposed between two clauses of the speech of the Jews. They were enjoining one another not to trust anyone if he was not a Jew; this is the first part. As for the second part, it is that they should not admit that anyone might be given the like of what the Children of Israel were given, since that would be an admission of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ. In this injunction which they enjoin upon one another is the utmost denial, disbelief and envy toward the Messenger and the Muslims alike.

safi-cedvel:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(يختصّ) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; (برحمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يختصّ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is هو. (الواو) conjunction; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (ذو) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw; (الفضل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (العظيم) naʿt (adjective) of الفضل, genitive like it.
The clause «يختصّ» is in the position of nominative as a third khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله) that occurs in the previous verse «[Note: It may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو.]».
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «الله ذو الفضل» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause (الله واسع) in the previous verse.

safi-cedvel:75-75.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (من أهل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (ان) a conditional particle making the verb jussive; (تأمن) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت; (بقنطار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأمن), the bāʾ having the meaning of على; (يؤدّ) an imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter from its end, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is هو; (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يؤدّ); (الواو) conjunction; (منهم من.. لا يؤدّه إليك) parsed like the beginning of the verse; (إلّا) a particle of restriction «[Note: Or a particle of exception, the noun excepted from being implied (muqaddar), namely all times, and the adverbial interpreted maṣdar is the excepted.]», (ما) a maṣdar particle of duration (maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya); (دمت) an incomplete past verb, mabnī on the sukūn.. and (التاء) is the ism of دام, in the position of nominative; (على) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (قائما), which is the khabar of دمت, accusative (manṣūb).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما دمت ...) is in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to the negated (يؤدّه) «[Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed (ما) to be merely maṣdariyya, with the interpreted maṣdar accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), so that it would be an exception from states, not from times, i.e.: except in the state of your constantly attending him; and (قائما) would then be a ḥāl, not a khabar, because دام has become complete.]».
(ذا) a demonstrative, mabnī, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address; (الباء) a preposition; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun, ism of أنّ, in the position of accusative; (قالوا) a past verb, mabnī on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم قالوا ...) is in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ, i.e.: that retreat from rendering the wealth is because of their belief as expressed.
(ليس) an incomplete past verb; (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar of the incomplete verb; (في الأميّين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar «[Note: It may also be attached to an omitted ḥāl of سبيل, because it is a description that preceded an indefinite noun it describes.]», the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (سبيل) the postponed ism of ليس, nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) resumptive; (يقولون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of الكذب «[Note: It may be attached to (يقولون), the verb being made to carry the meaning of يفترون (they fabricate).
(2, 3) i.e. the clause made up of the protasis and its apodosis.. and some are content with the conditional clause alone.]» «[Translator's note: The source has merged footnotes 2 and 3 (referenced below) into this footnote.]», (الكذب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) of the ḥāl; (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ; (يعلمون) like يقولون.
The clause «من أهل الكتاب من ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تأمنه (the first)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من) «2».
The clause «يؤدّه إليك» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a jussive condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «منهم من..» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive one.
The clause «تأمنه (the second)» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من) «3».
The clause «لا يؤدّه إليك» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a jussive condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «دمت» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قالوا» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of (أنّ).
The clause «ليس علينا..» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of the saying).
The clause «يقولون» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم يعلمون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(قنطار): a non-derived (jāmid) noun, its pattern فنعال (see verse 14 of this sūra).
(دينار): its original form is دنّار with a doubled nūn; pronouncing it with this nūn was found heavy, so the first of the two nūns was replaced by a yāʾ for lightness, because of frequent use; the doubling of the nūn returns in the broken plural, so one says دنانير, and in the diminutive, so one says دنينير.. and دينار is an Arabicized word.
(الكذب): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb كذب يكذب, of the ضرب class, its pattern فعل with fatḥa then kasra; it also comes with kasra on the first radical and sukūn on the second, and on the pattern فعال with kasra on the first radical and the second radical either single or doubled.

* Benefits:
1- The saying of the Jews «لَيْسَ عَلَيْنا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ»: this is what the Jews held at the time of the Messenger's mission, and this is what they still hold toward all the peoples of the world; they believe that wealth is their wealth which was usurped from them, and that they may recover it from people's hands by various means.
This mistaken notion has almost seeped into the common folk among the Muslims, whereas Islam forbade the Muslim to take anything of the wealth of followers of other religions except by right, so long as he is not in a state of war with those who oppose his religion.
2- The difference between «ما دام» and «ما زال» is that the first is inseparable from «ما» and comes only in the past form. As for the second, it can be in the past and the imperfect form, and it can also be preceded by one of the other negating particles, as in لم يزل and لا يزال.

safi-cedvel:76-76.t:
* I'rab:
(بلى) a particle of answer; it affirms what they negated in their saying (ليس علينا في الأميّين سبيل); (من) a conditional noun making the verb jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أوفى) a past verb, mabnī on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; (بعهد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أوفى), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction; (اتّقى) like أوفي and conjoined to it; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Name of Majesty, ism of إنّ, accusative (manṣūb); (يحبّ) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is هو; (المتّقين) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The clause من أوفى ... has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أوفى» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «اتّقى» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause أوفى.
The clause «إنّ الله يحب» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يحبّ المتّقين» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(أوفى): the verb contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution: the yāʾ was changed to alif because it came with a fatḥa after a fatḥa; its original form is أوفي — every verb whose first radical is wāw has yāʾ as its last radical.

* Benefits:
«بلى» is a particle of answer; it is specific to negation and conveys its cancellation, whether the negation is bare, as in «زَعَمَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ لَنْ يُبْعَثُوا قُلْ: بَلى وَرَبِّي لَتُبْعَثُنَّ», or joined with an interrogative, as in «أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْواهُمْ بَلى!». The difference between «بلى» and «نعم» is that بلى comes only after a negation, whereas نعم comes after negation and affirmation; so if you say «ما قام علي», confirming it is نعم and contradicting it is بلى ...

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(قل إن): their i'rab has already been given «[Note: In verse (29) of this sūra.]». (كنتم): an incomplete past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun of kāna, in the position of nominative. (تحبّون): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الله): the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الفاء): linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اتّبعوا): imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. the wāw is the fāʿil, (النون) is the nūn of protection, and (الياء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (يحبب): imperfect verb, jussive, as the response to the command, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الله): the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (الواو): conjunction. (يغفر): imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (يحبب), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (اللام): preposition, and (كم) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يغفر). (ذنوب): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو): resumptive. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (غفور): khabar (predicate), nominative. (رحيم): second khabar, nominative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إن كنتم تحبّون..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تحبّون الله» is in the position of accusative as the khabar of kāna.
The clause «اتّبعوني» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يحببكم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e. "if you follow me, Allah will love you".
The clause «الله غفور..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive, carrying the sense of causation.

* Rhetoric:
1- «يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ», i.e. He will be pleased with you, will bring you near to the precinct of His might, and will settle you in the neighbourhood of His holiness. This was expressed as love by way of metaphor (istiʿāra) or mushākala (verbal correspondence).

safi-cedvel:32-32.t:
* I'rab:
(قل): imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "أنت". (أطيعوا): imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الواو): conjunction. (الرسول): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, accusative like it. (الفاء): conjunction. (إن): jussive-governing conditional particle. (تولّوا): past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil «[Note: It may be an imperfect verb from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.]». (الفاء): linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb. (الله): the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative. (لا): negating. (يحبّ): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (الكافرين): mafʿūl bihi, accusative; the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «قل..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أطيعوا..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إن تولّوا» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying.
The clause «إنّ الله لا يحبّ..» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا يحبّ ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ..

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted, «فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا»: the i'rab of this verb is problematic, because the same word-form could be a past verb from the verb «تولّى» attributed to the wāw of the plural, or an imperfect verb of the "five verbs" («تتولون»), from which one of the two tāʾs has been deleted to lighten the word, made jussive by the conditional particle «إن», so the nūn of the nominative was dropped and it became «تولوا». The meaning of the verse is sound on both views, and the difference between them is confined to the presence or absence of «iltifāt (shift of person)».
2- His saying, the Exalted, «لا يحب»: the love of Allah is different from the love of servants, and this is a case of majāz mursal (metonymic trope). Love has dimensions and levels of perception. For the ordinary human being it is one of the laws of creation that Allah has placed in human nature, so that the creation that He, glory be to Him, made His vicegerent on His earth may continue. For the philosophers it has degrees, the highest of which is love of the True One who is worshipped, and it is this that prompts love of acts of obedience and of conformity [to His will].
For the Sufis it is the intoxication of witnessing, absorption at illumination, and annihilation in Allah at the hour of manifestation and union. And Allah knows best.

safi-cedvel:33-33.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ الله): its i'rab has already been given «[Note: In the previous verse.]». (اصطفى): past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (آدم): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); it does not take tanwīn because of being a proper name and foreign. (الواو): conjunction in the three places. (نوحا، آل، ال): nouns conjoined to آدم, accusative like it. (إبراهيم): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, as it is a diptote; and likewise (عمران). (على العالمين): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb اصطفى; the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ, as it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural.
The clause «إنّ الله اصطفى» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اصطفى» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(عمران): a proper name; it has been said to be foreign, and it has been said to be derived from العمر, with the alif and nūn in it being augments.
(نوحا): a foreign name with no derivation according to the meticulous grammarians; some claim it is derived from النوح (lamenting) and weeping. It is fully declinable because it is triliteral with a quiescent middle letter.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the verse there is the art of tawshīḥ, which, as Ibn Qudāma says in Naqd al-Shiʿr, is that there be at the beginning of the speech a meaning from which, once it is known, the rhyme is known. For from the meaning of the choosing of those mentioned in the verse the verse-ending (fāṣila) is known, because those mentioned are a class included within «العالمين».
«[Translator's note: Naqd al-Shiʿr is usually attributed to Qudāma ibn Jaʿfar; the text has "Ibn Qudāma".]»

safi-cedvel:34-34.t:
* I'rab:
(ذرّيّة): ḥāl (circumstantial) from آدم and what is conjoined to it, on the construal of a derived word «[Note: I.e. He chose them in the state of their branching from one another.. It may be a badal (substitute) from نوح or from the two آل.. and some make it a badal from آدم; that depends on the scholars' differing over the construal of the word ذرّيّة.]», accusative (manṣūb). (بعض): mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (ها) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (من بعض): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ بعض. (الواو): resumptive. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (سميع): khabar, nominative. (عليم): second khabar, nominative.
The clause «بعضها من بعض» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ذريّة.
The clause «الله سميع» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted, «ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُها مِنْ بَعْضٍ».
The word «بعض» is annexed to the overt noun and to the pronoun, and in both cases it is stripped of أل according to the rule of the muḍāf. For it is not permitted to make a muḍāf definite with أل when it is singular; so it is not correct to say «الكتاب الأستاذ» nor «القلم تلميذ». But أل may enter the dual, as when you say «المكرما سليم», and the sound masculine plural, as when you say «المكرمو علي» «[Note: See Jāmiʿ al-Durūs al-ʿArabiyya, vol. 3, p. 210.]».

safi-cedvel:35-35.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ): an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر". (قال): past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine. (امرأة): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (عمران): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa, as it is a diptote. (ربّ): a vocative in construct (munādā muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb), from which the vocative particle has been omitted; the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, its appearance being prevented by the place being occupied by the vowel suited [to the yāʾ], and (the yāʾ of the first person), which is omitted, is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الياء) is a pronoun, the noun of إنّ. (نذرت): past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء) is the fāʿil. (اللام): preposition, and (الكاف) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نذرت). (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (في بطن): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما; the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (محرّرا): ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the relative noun. (الفاء): conjunction, linking the effect to the cause — or linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. (تقبّل): an imperative verb of supplication, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (من): preposition, and (الياء) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تقبّل). (إنّك): like إنّي. (أنت): a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «[Note: Or a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar is لسميع, the [whole] khabar being the khabar of إنّ.]» «[Translator's note: the text reads "لسميع"; the verse has السَّمِيعُ without a lām.]». (السميع): the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative. (العليم): second khabar, nominative.
The clause «قالت امرأة عمران..» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «the vocative and what is within its scope» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّي نذرت» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «نذرت لك.» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «تقبّل منّي» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause إنّي نذرت; or it is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if You are pleased with me, then accept from me".
The clause «إنّك أنت السميع» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(امرأة): a primitive (jāmid) noun of entity, feminine of امرئ; its plural is نساء or نسوة, from a different root. The definite article (ال) rarely enters امرأة, so one says (المرأة). Its pattern is افعلة with fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(محرّرا): passive participle from the quadriliteral verb حرّر; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء): resumptive. (لمّا): an adverb meaning "when", containing the sense of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قالت). (وضعت): past verb.. (التاء) is for the feminine, (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هي". (قالت): like وضعت. (ربّ إنّى وضعت): like ربّ إنّي نذرت in the previous verse, and (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (أننى): ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb), from the pronoun of the absent feminine. (الواو): parenthetical. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (أعلم): khabar (predicate), nominative. (الباء): preposition. (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (أعلم). (وضعت): like the first. (الواو): conjunction. (ليس): an incomplete, invariable (jāmid) past verb. (الذكر): the noun of ليس, nominative. (كالأنثى): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of ليس. (الواو): conjunction. إنّي سميت): like في نذرت «[Translator's note: so in the text; the intended sense is "like إنّي نذرت".]», and (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (مريم): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; it does not take tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine. (الواو): conjunction. (إني أعيذ): like إنّي نذرت; (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الواو): conjunction. (ذرّيّة): conjoined to the accusative pronoun in عيذها «[Translator's note: so in the text, for أعيذها.]», and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (من الشيطان): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb أعيذ. (الرجيم): naʿt (adjective) of الشيطان, genitive (majrūr) like it.
The clause «وضعتها» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قالت..» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «the vocative and what is within its scope» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّي وضعتها..» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «وضعتها أنثى» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «الله أعلم» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The clause «وضعت» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «ليس الذكر كالأنثى» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to.
the vocative «1».
The clause «إنّي سمّيتها..» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative «2».
«[Translator's note: the footnote markers «1» and «2» have no corresponding footnote text in the source, and the sentence "conjoined to. the vocative" is broken as printed.]»
The clause «سمّيتها مريم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّي أعيذها ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative.
The clause «أعيذها» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(أعلم): a derived adjective on the pattern أفعل, not for the elative (tafḍīl); it means عالم or عليم.
(الرجيم): a derived adjective on the pattern فعيل with the meaning of مفعول, i.e. المرجوم (the stoned), meaning the one expelled from the mercy of Allah.
(الذكر): a derived adjective on the pattern فعل with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
1- «قالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعْتُها أُنْثى»: the purpose of the statement is regret. The aim of this speech is not to inform, because informing is either for conveying the information (fāʾidat al-khabar) or its corollary (lāzim al-fāʾida), and the knowledge of Allah the Exalted encompasses both; so it is merely for expressing regret and grief.
2- What is intended by the statement in His saying, the Exalted, «وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما وَضَعَتْ» is the corollary of the information; what is intended is not to rebut her in her reporting of what He, glory be to Him, knows better, as might appear from the context. Rather the clause is «parenthetical», brought to magnify the newborn she had delivered, to exalt its status, and to point out her ignorance of [His] power — i.e. "Allah knows best the thing she delivered, and the great matters, subtle secrets and clear signs connected with it", while she was heedless of all that.
3- «وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُها بِكَ»: here the khabar of إنّ was brought as an imperfect verb, to indicate her seeking the continuation of the benefit without interruption; this is unlike «وضعتها» and «وسميتها», where the two predicates were brought as past verbs because they were concluded. The one in whom refuge is sought was placed before the conjoined element that follows, out of concern for it.
4- «وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ كَالْأُنْثى» is another parenthesis, explaining the magnification contained in the first; it is not an explanation of its explicit wording, such that it would be treated like ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), in which conjunction is not permitted.
5- Iṭnāb (amplification): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُها مَرْيَمَ».
Her aim in presenting it to the Knower of the unseen was to draw near to Him, the Exalted, and to seek protection for her — for Maryam in their language means "the worshipper", and al-Qurṭubī said: its meaning is "servant of the Lord" — and to show that she was not going back on her intention, even though what she had delivered was female, and that even if she was not fit for the custodianship of Bayt al-Maqdis, let her be among the worshippers in it.
6- His saying «وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِما وَضَعَتْ» is an iltifāt (shift of person) from the second person to the third, to show the utmost reverence.

* Benefits:
1- The name Maryam in their language at that time was «the worshipper». The daughter of ʿImrān was given this name in the hope and desire that she would be among the worshippers. And her saying "I have named her Maryam": this statement is for the corollary of the information; informing Allah of the naming is not intended, since He knows that best.
2- On His saying, the Exalted, «قالَتْ رَبِّ»..
When the word annexed to the yāʾ of the first person is أب or أم, three usages are permitted in it. The first:
يا أب and يا أمّ, with deletion of the yāʾ; the second, يا أبي and يا أمي; and the third, يا أبا and يا أما. It is also permitted in them to delete the yāʾ of the first person and compensate for it with the tāʾ of the feminine, e.g. يا أبت and يا أمت and يا أبت and يا أمت «[Translator's note: the forms are repeated as printed; the vowelling that distinguishes them (yā abati / yā abata) is not shown in the text.]», and it is permitted to replace this tāʾ with the hāʾ of pausing, e.g. يا أبه and يا أمّه. Close to that is the annexation of the word «الرب» to the yāʾ of the first person: you say يا ربّ and يا ربّ, and it is permitted to delete the vocative yāʾ, so you say ربّ and ربّ; the first is according to the dialect of one who does not await [the rest of the word], and the second according to one who awaits it. And if we say يا ربّ, it is according to the dialect of one who awaits its annexation to something other than the yāʾ of the first person, like «يا ربّ العباد».
«[Translator's note: the paired forms of ربّ are printed identically; the distinction intended (e.g. rabbi / rabbu) depends on vowelling not shown in the text.]»

safi-cedvel:37-37.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء): resumptive. (تقبّل): past verb, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (ربّ): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (ها) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الباء): a redundant (zāʾida) preposition «[Note: Or an original preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to (تقبّلها), the bāʾ being for seeking help.. Abū Ḥayyān said: القبول is a noun for that by which a thing is accepted, like السعوط for that by which snuff is administered.]». (قبول): genitive in form, accusative in position, mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), standing in for the maṣdar because it meets it in derivation. (حسن): naʿt (adjective) of قبول, genitive in form like it. (الواو): conjunction. (أنبتها): like تقبّلها. (نباتا): mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar because it meets it in derivation. (حسنا): naʿt of (نباتا), accusative (manṣūb) like it. (الواو): conjunction. (كفّلها): like تقبّلها. (زكريّا): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied on the alif. (كلّما): a conditional adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis وجد «[Note: The apodosis may be قال, with the clause وجد a ḥāl (circumstantial).]».. and ما is a maṣdar particle. (دخل): past verb. (على): preposition, and (ها) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (دخل). (زكريّا): fāʿil, nominative; the sign of the nominative is the ḍamma implied on the alif. (المحراب): mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-tawassuʿ) «[Note: Because (دخل) is made transitive with one of the two particles (في) or (إلى).]». (وجد): like دخل. (عند): adverb of place, attached to (وجد) «[Note: It may be attached to an omitted ḥāl from (رزقا).]», and (ها) is muḍāf ilayhi. (رزقا): mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما دخل) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "every time of entering".
(قال): like دخل. (يا): vocative particle. (مريم): a vocative of a single proper name (munādā mufrad ʿalam), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative. (أنّي): an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). (اللام): preposition, and (الكاف) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the omitted khabar. (ها): particle of alerting. (ذا): a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (قالت): past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine. (هو): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (من عند): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar. (الله): the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb. (الله): the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative. (يرزق): imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (من): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (يشاء): like يرزق. (بغير): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl «[Note: See verse (27) of this sūra and the various possibilities for attaching the preposition and its genitive noun.]». (حساب): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «تقبّلها ربّها» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أنبتها» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفّلها» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «دخل عليها» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative.
The clause «وجد» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يا مريم..» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أنّي لك هذا» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «قالت ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هو من عند الله» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying.
The clause «إنّ الله يرزق ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive «[Note: The clause may be part of the completion of Maryam's saying, and it may be from the speech of Allah the Exalted.]».
The clause «يرزق من يشاء» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (من).

* Morphology:
(قبول): it has the form of a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); the qāf may be given fatḥa or ḍamma.. or it is the maṣdar of the triliteral قبل; its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(حسن): an assimilate adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha); its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas; its verb is حسن يحسن, of the كرم class (see al-Baqara 245).
(نباتا): a noun of the maṣdar from أنبت, whose regular maṣdar is إنبات; the pattern of نبات is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(زكريّا): it is the shortened form of زكرياء, whose hamza is for the feminine.
(المحراب): a noun of place, irregularly formed; its pattern is مفعال with kasra on the mīm, and its verb is حارب. It is any place in which Satan is fought, reserved for worship.

* Rhetoric:
1- Al-jinās al-mughāyir (paronomasia between different word-classes): in His saying «فَتَقَبَّلَها رَبُّها بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ», in His saying «وَأَنْبَتَها نَباتاً حَسَناً», and in His saying «رزقا» and «يرزق».
2- «فتقبلها», i.e. He was pleased with Maryam in the vow in place of a male.
In it the vow is likened to a gift, and the good pleasure of Allah the Exalted to acceptance.
3- «وأنبتها» is a figure for raising her with what was good for her in all her states. It is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) with the relation of concomitance, for the cultivator tends his crop by watering it when it needs it, protecting it from blights and uprooting the plants that choke it.
4- Al-ishāra (allusion), which is expressing a hidden meaning with an overt word, in His saying «هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ», i.e. it is a provision that none but Allah brings at that time.
5- Indefiniteness: in His saying «رزقا», to convey diffusion and abundance, and that it was not of one kind but of many kinds.

* Benefits:
1- «كلّما»: when «ما» is joined to the word «كل», «ما» is parsed as an adverbial maṣdar particle. This joining is found in the rules of Arabic orthography in writing. Of this kind is the joining of «the nominal ما» to the word «سيّ», as in «أحب أصدقائي ولا سيما زهير» (I love my friends, especially Zuhayr); [and to نعم] when its ʿayn takes kasra, as in «نعمّا يعظكم به», but when its ʿayn is quiescent separation is obligatory, as in «نعم ما تفعل». They have joined the redundant particle «ما», whatever its kind, to what precedes it, as in «طالما نصحت لك» (how often I have advised you), «أَنَّما إِلهُكُمْ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ», «أتيت لكنما اسامة لم يأت» (I came, but Usāma did not come), «عند ما تجتهد تنجح» (when you strive you succeed), «عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نادِمِينَ», «مِمَّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا», «أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ», «أينما تجلس اجلس» (wherever you sit I will sit), «إمّا تجتهد تنجح» (if you strive you succeed), «إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِثْلَ ما أَنَّكُمْ تَنْطِقُونَ» and «اجتهد كيما تنجح» (strive so that you may succeed). They have joined the maṣdar ما to the word «مثل», the word «ريث», the word «حين» and the word «كل»; after the word «كل» in particular it is an adverbial maṣdar particle.
«[Translator's note: "[and to نعم]" is added for clarity; the text passes directly from «سيّ» to "when its ʿayn takes kasra". Note also that «عند ما» is printed separated although cited as an example of joining.]»

safi-cedvel:184-184.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (كذّبوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of a jussive ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (كذّب) a passive past verb; (رسل) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of رسل, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (جاؤوا) like كذّبوا, having no position; (بالبينّات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جاؤوا); (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (الزبر، الكتاب) two nouns conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the two conjunctions to البيّنات, genitive (majrūr) like it; (المنير) naʿt of الكتاب, genitive.
The clause «كذبوك» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قل in the previous verse; the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "then be patient as messengers before you were patient", or "then take consolation".
The clause «قد كذّب رسل» has no grammatical position: a causal explanation (taʿlīl) of the implied apodosis, because the verb is past in both wording and meaning.
The clause «جاؤوا ...» has no grammatical position, nominative, naʿt of رسل «[Translator's note: so in the source: «لا محلّ لها رفع نعت لرسل». The two statements conflict; as a naʿt of the indefinite رسل the clause would be in the position of a nominative.]».

* Morphology:
(زبر) plural of زبور. Its origin is from الزبر, i.e. restraining (al-zajr). The book containing wisdom was called زبور because it restrains (yazburu), i.e. it restrains from falsehood and calls to the truth. In al-Mukhtār: الزبر is restraining and rebuking, of the pattern (bāb) نصر; الزبر is also writing, of the pattern ضرب. The wazn of زبور is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and الزبر is فعل with two ḍammas.
(المنير) active participle from the quadriliteral أنار; its wazn is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn, and it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by vowel-removal (taskīn).

safi-cedvel:185-185.t:
* I'rab:
(كل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (نفس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (ذائقة) khabar (predicate), nominative, and (الموت) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) a conjunction; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (توفّون) a passive imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (أجور) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (توفّون); (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الفاء) a conjunction; (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; (زحزح) a passive past verb, its deputy agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (عن النار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (زحزح); (الواو) a conjunction; (أدخل) like زحزح; (الجنّة) a direct object, accusative by way of latitude (ʿalā al-saʿa) «[Note: The basic usage of the verb (أدخل) is that it reaches, along with the explicit object, a second object through the preposition إلى. When the verb was made passive, the transitivity through the preposition إلى remained; then the preposition was dropped because of frequent use — or latitude — so the noun (الجنّة) became accusative as an object.]»; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (فاز) a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) a latent pronoun, implied as "huwa". (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative, inoperative (muhmala); (الحياة) mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الدنيا) naʿt (adjective) of الحياة, nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the alif; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (متاع) the khabar of الحياة, nominative; (الغرور) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «كلّ نفس ذائقة.» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «توفّون أجوركم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «من زحزح (the nominal clause)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «زحزح ...» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together ...]».
The clause «أدخل ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause زحزح.
The clause «قد فاز» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «الحياة ... متاع» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ذائقة) the feminine of ذائق «[Note: The word (ذائقة) is made feminine so as to refer back to كلّ نفس, which carries the meaning of a plural. It is said that the meaning of النفس here is the body, not the spirit, for it is the body that dies and not the spirit.. It is also said that the soul (al-nafs) dies, as evidenced by this verse ... and this is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān, for it is stated in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ: "Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar al-Rāzī said: in this verse is an indication that the soul does not die with the death of the body, and that the soul is other than the body — end quote. This is obstinacy regarding the indication, for the apparent meaning of the verse indicates that the soul dies." End quote.]». It is the active participle from ذاق يذوق, of the pattern (bāb) نصر; the weak letter was changed into a hamza because it comes after the alif of فاعل, regularly; the original is ذاوق.
(توفّون) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion; its original is توفّاون, with sukūn on the second wāw. Two quiescent letters met, so the alif was deleted to escape that, and the fāʾ remained with fatḥa to indicate the deleted letter. Its wazn is تفعّون with ḍamma on the tāʾ and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(فاز) it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (qalb); its original is فوز: the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. Its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
- «إِلَّا مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ»: an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh). Allah, Glorified and Exalted, likened this world to goods by which the prospective buyer is deceived and lured until he buys them, after which their corruption and inferiority become clear to him. Satan is the deceiving beguiler. This is for whoever prefers it over the Hereafter; as for whoever seeks the Hereafter through it, it is goods that bring one to the destination (matāʿ balāgh).

* Benefits:
1- The saying of the Exalted: «وَإِنَّما تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ».
We discussed earlier «ما» when «إنّ or one of its sisters» is attached to it, and that it is parsed as kāffa wa-makfūfa. Returning to it, we mention this benefit.
If the «ما» attached to these particles is a relative noun or a maṣdar-forming particle, it does not restrain them from governing; rather they remain governing the accusative of the noun and the nominative of the khabar, as in the saying of the Exalted: «ما عِنْدَكُمْ يَنْفَدُ» «[Translator's note: the verse as quoted contains no inna or sister; the author's point concerns «إنّ ما» written separately.]»: ما here is a relative noun in the position of an accusative, its noun, and the clause «ينفد» is in the position of a nominative, its khabar. As for your saying:
«إنّ ما تستقيم حسن» (your being upright is good): «ما» here is maṣdar-forming, interpreted with the verb as a maṣdar, and this maṣdar is in the position of an accusative as the noun of inna, and «حسن» is its khabar, i.e. إن استقامتك حسنة.
You may have noticed that «ما» is written separately from «إنّ» when it is a relative noun or maṣdar-forming.
The maṣdar-forming ما and the restraining ما have come together in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فلو أن أسعى لأدنى معيشة ... كفاني ولم أطلب قليل من المال
(Were it that I strove for the lowest livelihood, a little wealth would suffice me and I would not seek [more].)
فلو ان ما أسعى لمجد مؤثل ... وقد يدرك المجد المؤثل أمثالي
(Were it that I strove for deep-rooted glory — and the likes of me may attain deep-rooted glory.)
«[Translator's note: the verses are printed thus in the source. The first line lacks «ما» («فلو أن أسعى»), and the second line is printed «فلو ان ما أسعى», whereas the author's explanation below assumes «ما» in the first line and «لكنما» in the second.]»
So ما in the first line is maṣdar-forming, the implied meaning being «لو أنّ سعيي» (were it that my striving), and in the second line it is redundant and restraining, i.e. «but I strive for deep-rooted glory». So reflect, for in it there is enjoyment for specialists.

safi-cedvel:186-186.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) occurring in the response to an implied (muqaddar) oath; (تبلونّ) a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the presence of the nūn, which was deleted because of the succession of identical letters (tawālī al-amthāl) ... and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of a nominative, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) ... and the nūn is the nūn of emphasis, having no position; (في اموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تبلونّ), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (أنفس) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أموال, genitive (majrūr) like it, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (تسمعنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the presence of the nūn, deleted because of the succession of identical letters ... and the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent) ... and (النون) is the heavy nūn of emphasis; (من) a preposition; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (تسمعنّ); (أوتوا) a passive past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma ... and the wāw is the deputy agent; (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the deputy agent, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (من الذين) like the first, attached to what the first is attached to, so it is conjoined to it; (أشركوا) a past verb ... and its agent; (أذى) a direct object governed by تسمعنّ, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on the alif; (كثيرا) naʿt (adjective) of أذى, accusative like it. (الواو) resumptive; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (تصبروا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the agent; (الواو) a conjunction; (تتّقوا) like تصبروا and conjoined to it; (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, the noun of inna, and the (اللام) is for distance and the (الكاف) for address; (من عزم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna; (الأمور) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «تبلون» has no grammatical position: the response to an implied oath.
The clause «تسمعنّ» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تبلونّ.
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أشركوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إن تصبروا» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تتّقوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تصبروا.
The clause «إنّ ذلك من عزم..» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(تبلونّ) this wāw is the wāw of the pronoun, not the final radical (lām) of the word. Its original is تبلاون — with sukūn on the wāw, before the nūn of emphasis entered the verb. Two quiescent letters met, so the alif was deleted and it became تبلون — with fatḥa on the lām and sukūn on the wāw. When the nūn of emphasis entered, the nūn of the nominative was deleted for lightness because of the succession of identical letters, and it became تبلونّ — with sukūn on the wāw and a doubled nūn. Then the wāw was given ḍamma to escape the meeting of two quiescent letters, namely the wāw and the first nūn of the nūn of emphasis, and it became تبلونّ. As for (تسمعنّ), it is the agent pronoun that is deleted ... and the verb underwent the same deletion of the sign of the nominative as in تبلونّ.
(عزم) a hearsay-based (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb عزم يعزم, of the pattern (bāb) ضرب; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn. There are other maṣdars: عزم with ḍamma on the ʿayn; معزم with fatḥa on the mīm and the zāy, or kasra on the zāy; عزيم and عزمة with fatḥa on the ʿayn and the zāy; and عزيمة and عزمان with ḍamma on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- We pointed out previously that the nūn of the nominative of the imperfect verb attached to the wāw of the plural is deleted when it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, because of the succession of identical letters. It may be useful to comment here on this feature of our Arabic language — and how many its features are! The feature of lightening the burden on the tongue and easing pronunciation is a general and deep-rooted phenomenon covering many aspects of our language, and deletion because of the succession of identical letters is one aspect of this feature, whether it is the succession of nūns in the example «[Note: Likewise the deletion of the wāw of the plural because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, for the aim of this deletion is to ease pronunciation and to turn from difficulty to ease.]» mentioned above, or the succession of tāʾs at the start of an imperfect verb beginning with a tāʾ followed by the tāʾ of the imperfect, so that one of them is deleted because of the succession of identical letters. Were we to trace the places of easing in this language, we would go beyond the plan of the study, for they are many. Whoever wishes to enjoy them and learn their course should seek them in their place in the books of grammar, morphology and philology (fiqh al-lugha); it is a delightful and useful study.

safi-cedvel:155-155.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الذين) a relative noun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; (تولّوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, which was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (من) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent pronoun; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (تولّوا); (التقى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif; (الجمعان) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the alif; (إنّما) a restraining particle and the particle restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa); (استزل) a past verb, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الشيطان) fāʿil, nominative; (ببعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استزل); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (كسبوا) a past verb and its fāʿil. (الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (عفا) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (عنهم) like منكم, attached to (عفا); (إنّ) like the first one; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (غفور) khabar (predicate), nominative; (حليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إنّ الذين تولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تولّوا منكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «التقى الجمعان» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «استزلّهم الشيطان» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «كسبوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «عفا الله..» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور» has no grammatical position, being resumptive and giving a reason.

* Morphology:
(الجمعان): the dual of الجمع, which is a noun for a gathering of people; its verb is جمع يجمع, of the fataḥa class (bāb fataḥa); its pattern is فعل, with a fatḥa followed by a sukūn.

* Benefits:
1- «إِنَّمَا اسْتَزَلَّهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ»: it is agreed that the redundant «ما» restrains inna and its sisters from governing, so that what follows it reverts to being a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar. But when the «ما» attached to «inna and its sisters» is a relative noun or a maṣdar particle, it does not restrain them from governing; rather they remain putting the noun in the accusative and the khabar in the nominative.
If «ما» is a relative noun, it is in the position of accusative as its noun, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ما عِنْدَكُمْ يَنْفَدُ», i.e. "indeed, that which is with you runs out" «[Translator's note: the source illustrates with this verse, which in the muṣḥaf does not contain إنّ.]»; and if «ما» is a maṣdar particle, then ما and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of accusative as the noun of inna, as in «إن ما تستقيم حسن», i.e. "your being upright is good". In these two cases «ما» is written separately, unlike the restraining «ما», which is written joined, as in the verse. The maṣdar ما and the restraining ما have come together in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فلو أن ما أسعى لأدنى معيشة ... كفاني ولم أطلب قليل من المال
ولكنما أسعى لمجد مؤثّل ... وقد يدرك المجد المؤثّل أمثالي
(If what I strove for were the barest livelihood, a little wealth would suffice me and I would not seek more; but I strive for deep-rooted glory, and the likes of me may attain deep-rooted glory.)

safi-cedvel:156-156.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative, and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from أيّ - following it in its position - or a naʿt (adjective) of it; (آمنوا) a verb and its fāʿil (agent); (لا) the prohibitive, jussivizing lā; (تكونوا) a deficient imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the noun of kāna; (الكاف) a preposition; (الذين) a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of تكون; (كفروا) like آمنوا; (الواو) conjunction; (قالوا) like آمنوا; (لإخوان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قالوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إذا) an adverb of future time, borrowed here for the past and encompassing the present and the future; it is stripped of the sense of condition and is attached to (قالوا); (ضربوا) like آمنوا; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ضربوا); (أو) a conjunction; (كانوا) a deficient past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and (الواو) is the noun of kāna; (غزّى) the khabar of كانوا, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (لو) a non-jussivizing conditional particle; (كانوا) like the first one; (عند) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the omitted khabar of كانوا, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ما) negative; (ماتوا) like آمنوا; (الواو) conjunction; (ما قتلوا) ما is negative, and a past verb in the passive, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (اللام) of causation (taʿlīl) - or the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba) -; (يجعل) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (حسرة) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt of حسرة, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يجعل.) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (قالوا).. i.e. they said that so that He might put regret into their hearts.. or they said that, and the consequence and outcome of their saying was regret and remorse.
(الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (يحيي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (الواو) conjunction; (يميت) like يحيي, with the ḍamma overt; (الواو) conjunction; (الله) like the first one; (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to بصير «[Note: It is permissible for (ما) to be a maṣdar particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by the preposition.]»; (تعملون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (بصير) the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative.
The vocative clause «يأيّها ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تكونوا..» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «قالوا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كفروا.
The clause «ضربوا» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «كانوا غزّى» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause ضربوا.
The clause «لو كانوا عندنا» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb "to say" (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ما ماتوا» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition.
The clause «ما قتلوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما ماتوا.
The clause «يجعل الله» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the maṣdar relative particle (أن).
The clause «الله يحيي..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحيي» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «يميت» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause يحيي.
The clause «الله.. بصير» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause الله يحيي.
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(غزّى): plural of غاز; by analogy it would be pluralised as غزاة, just as رام has the plural رماة, but the weak verb was treated like the sound one, as with ضارب and ضرّب ...
غاز is originally الغازي; the yāʾ is changed from a wāw because it is vowelless and preceded by a kasra, and the yāʾ was dropped because of the tanwīn.. The original of غزّى is غزّو: the wāw was changed into an alif because it was vowelled and preceded by a fatḥa, then the alif was dropped in pronunciation to suit the tanwīn.

* Rhetoric:
1- «إِذا ضَرَبُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ»: the preference for إذا, which conveys the sense of the future, over إذ, which conveys the sense of the past, is for narrating a past state (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl al-māḍiya), since what is meant by it is continuous time encompassing the present, around which the evoking of the scene revolves. This is a splendid art among the arts of rhetoric.
2- Ṭibāq (antithesis): between يحيي and يميت; it is among the most concise and truthful of speech and the most far-reaching in indicating the intended meaning.
3- «وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ»: using the majestic Name overtly where a pronoun would be expected, in order to instil awe, cast dread, intensify the threat and make the warning severe.

* Benefits:
1- In this verse there is a foreshadowing that appointed terms of life are fixed, and that courage does not bring one's term nearer and cowardice does not put it off. Al-Manfalūṭī reversed this kind of cowards' thinking and said:
«Death is more frequent in retreat than in advance». And the Sword of Allah, Khālid ibn al-Walīd, alluded to this meaning in his saying, while on his deathbed, words to the effect: «I have plunged into battle after battle until there is no span-wide spot left on my body without a spear-thrust or a sword-blow in it, and here I am dying on my bed as a camel dies; so may the eyes of cowards never sleep».
2- The lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra) is nothing but one of the lāms of causation, except that it indicates the end and consequence of a thing. Its ruling in i'rab is like the ruling of the lām of causation: it puts the imperfect verb in the accusative by an «أن» that may optionally be implied after it.

safi-cedvel:157-157.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) preparing for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (إن) a jussivizing conditional particle; (قتلتم) a past verb in the passive, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) a pronoun, nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قتلتم); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أو) a conjunction; (متّم) like قتلتم; (اللام) occurring in the answer to an oath; (مغفرة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) «1» «[Translator's note: the footnote marker «1» appears in the source without its footnote text.]»; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of مغفرة; (الواو) conjunction; (رحمة) conjoined to مغفرة, nominative like it; (خير) khabar (predicate), nominative; (من) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun «2» «[Translator's note: footnote «2» is likewise missing in the source.]» indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to خير; (يجمعون) an imperfect verb, nominative ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent).
The clause «قتلتم..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «متّم..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قتلتم.
The clause «مغفرة.. خير» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an oath.
The clause «يجمعون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).

* Morphology:
(متمّ): it involves a phonetic change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) to suit the indeclinability on the sukūn; its original form is موتّم: the weak letter was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. Its pattern is فلتم, with a ḍamma on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
1- The lām preparing for the oath: it usually enters upon the conditional particle «إن», announcing that the answer after it is built on an oath before it and not on the condition, as in «لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُوا لا يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ وَلَئِنْ قُوتِلُوا لا يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ». If the oath is stated, the lām is not required before the conditional particle, as in «والله إن أكرمتني لأكرمنّك» ("By Allah, if you honour me I will surely honour you"); it is usually required when the oath is omitted, and it is rarely omitted along with the omission of the oath, as in «وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنا وَتَرْحَمْنا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ», and it was said that it is «عفوية» (spontaneous) in such cases «[Translator's note: so in the source; the intended word is unclear, perhaps "implied" (مقدّرة).]».

safi-cedvel:158-158.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (لئن متّم أو قتلتم) like the previous verse; (اللام) occurring in the answer to an oath; (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تحشرون), which is an imperfect verb in the passive, nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «متّم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «قتلتم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause متّم.
The clause «تحشرون» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an oath.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse and the one before it there is an orderly art in the matter of fronting and postponement (al-taqdīm wa-l-taʾkhīr): death and being killed occur in them three times; death is placed before being killed in the first and last of them, and being killed is placed before death in the middle one, in accordance with placing first what is more important and more noble.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(هو الذي) its i'rab has been given before «[Note: in the preceding ayah (6).]»; (أنزل) a past verb, and the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (على) a preposition, and (الكاف) an attached pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنزل); (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (من) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) «[Note: Or attached to a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: "the first part of it" or "the first portion of it", and آيات is the khabar.]»; (آيات) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (محكمات) naʿt of آيات, nominative like it; (هن) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أمّ) khabar, nominative «[Note: The singular is used as predicate of the plural because He meant that each ayah of it is the Mother of the Book, or that its ayahs, by their precision and cohesion, are like a single ayah which is the Mother of the Book.]»; (الكتاب) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (أخر) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to آيات, nominative like it «[Note: It is originally a naʿt of an implied (آيات), and the adjective has taken the place of the noun it qualifies.]», and it is barred from tanwīn (a diptote) because of being an adjective and because of ʿadl (deflection from its original form); (متشابهات) naʿt of أخر, nominative like it; (الفاء) resumptive; (أمّا) a particle of condition and detailing; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (زيغ) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of the condition أمّا; (يتّبعون) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (تشابه) a past verb, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (منه) like the first, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of تشابه; (ابتغاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative; (الفتنة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (ابتغاء تأويل) like ابتغاء الفتنة, and conjoined to it, accusative like it; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (ما) negative; (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative; (تأويل) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء), here and in the previous one, is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (الراسخون) maʿṭūf to the Name of Majesty, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw «[Note: It is permissible to make the wāw resumptive and (الراسخون) a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause يقولون آمنّا. This ayah [Translator's note: i.e. this clause] is a substitute for repeating (أمّا) and what follows it, as though the original were to be said: "and as for others, they believe in it, [entrusting] its meaning to their Lord."]»; (في العلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (الراسخون); (يقولون) like يتّبعون; (آمنّا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) is the fāʿil; (به) like منه, attached to (آمنا); (كلّ) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and the tanwīn is for compensation; (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ كلّ; (ربّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (يذكّر) an imperfect verb, nominative; (إلّا) a particle of restriction; (أولو) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw, for it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (الألباب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «هو الذي أنزل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «أنزل عليك الكتاب» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «منه آيات» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl of الكتاب.
The clause «هنّ أم الكتاب» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl of آيات, or in the position of a nominative as naʿt of آيات.
The clause «الذين في قلوبهم زيغ» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «في قلوبهم زيغ» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يتّبعون» is in the position of a nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين), and it is the response of أمّا.
The clause «تشابه منه» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يعلم تأويله ...» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl.
The clause «يقولون» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl of (الراسخون).
The clause «آمنّا به» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كلّ من عند ربّنا» is in the position of an accusative as badal (substitute) of the clause آمنّا به «[Note: This clause falls within the scope of the saying, so it is the speech reported in meaning, and it is not linked to the preceding clause by a conjunction.]».
The clause «ما يذّكّر إلّا أولو الألباب» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(محكمات): plural of محكمة, the feminine of محكم, a passive participle of the quadriliteral أحكم; its wazn is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(متشابهات): plural of متشابه, feminine of متشابه [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "plural of متشابهة, feminine of متشابه"], an active participle of the five-letter verb تشابه; its wazn is متفاعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
