(لربّ): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اقنتي), and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الواو): conjunction in both places. (اسجدي، اركعي): like اقنتي. (مع): adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the verb اركعي. (الراكعين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ.
The clause «the vocative and what is within its scope» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اقنتي لربّك» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «اسجدي» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اقنتي.
The clause «اركعي» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اقنتي.

* Rhetoric:
1- «يا مَرْيَمُ»: the repetition of the vocative is to announce that what is intended by the address is what comes after it, and that the reminder of blessings before it was a preparation for mentioning it and an encouragement to act according to it.
2- «وَاسْجُدِي وَارْكَعِي مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ», fronting (taqdīm): prostration was placed before bowing, either because that was the order in their sacred law, or because prostration is the most excellent pillar of the prayer and the utmost degree of submission.

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(ذا): a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (الكاف) is a particle of address and (اللام) is for distance. (من أنباء): preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (الغيب): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (نوحي): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma; (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), in the position of accusative, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن", for majesty. (إلى): preposition, and (الكاف) is a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نوحيه). (الواو): conjunction. (ما): negating. (كنت): an incomplete past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء) is the noun of kāna. (لدي): adverb of place, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative, attached to the omitted khabar of kāna, and (هم) is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (إذ): an adverb for past time, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to the omitted khabar. (يلقون): imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (أقلام): mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi. (أيّ): an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi. (يكفل): imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (مريم): mafʿūl bihi, accusative; it is prevented from tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine. (الواو): conjunction. (ما كنت لديهم إذ): like the first. (يختصمون): like يلقون.
The clause «ذلك من أنباء الغيب» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «نوحيه» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الغيب.
The clause «ما كنت لديهم» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يلقون..» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أيّهم يكفل..» is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb.
The clause «يكفل..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أيّهم.
The clause «ما كنت لديهم (the second)» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first.
The clause «يختصمون» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

* Morphology:
(أنباء): plural of نبأ, which is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from أنبأ or نبّأ; the regular maṣdar of the two verbs would be إنباء — with kasra on the first hamza — or تنبئ. The pattern of نبأ is فعل with two fatḥas.
(يلقون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, following the same course as تلفوا «[Translator's note: so in the text; تلقوا is evidently intended.]» (see verse 195 of Sūrat al-Baqara).
(أقلامهم): plural of قلم, a primitive (jāmid) noun of entity; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
1- «إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلامَهُمْ», i.e. they cast them and threw them down to draw lots, by way of kināya (metonymy), i.e. a metonymy for the lot.

safi-cedvel:190-191.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (في خلق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of (إنّ); (السموات) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الأرض) conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw to السموات, genitive like it; (الواو) a conjunction; (اختلاف) conjoined to خلق, genitive like it; (الليل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (النهار) conjoined by the wāw to الليل, genitive like it; (اللام) the lām of emphasis; (آيات) the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (لأولي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آيات, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; (الألباب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause ... has no grammatical position: resumptive.
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, naʿt of أولي — or a badal (substitute) from it — «[Note: It may be cut off from qualification and made the khabar of a necessarily omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم", or be in the position of an accusative by way of praise.]»; (يذكرون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (قياما) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative «[Note: If the verb يذكرون is made to include the meaning of يصلّون (they pray), i.e. they stand and sit, then قياما is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar. But if (قياما وقعودا) are plurals of قائم and قاعد, they are ḥāls and nothing else.]»; (قعودا) conjoined by the wāw to (قياما), accusative like it; (الواو) a conjunction; (على جنوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the pronoun of يذكرون, and it is conjoined to the first explicit ḥāl, i.e. and lying on their sides, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (يتفكّرون) like يذكرون; (في خلق) like the first, attached to (يتفكّرون); (السموات والأرض) like the first; (ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), annexed, with the vocative particle omitted, accusative, and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ما) negative; (خلقت) a past verb and its agent; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, direct object; (باطلا) a ḥāl, accusative «[Note: al-Zamakhsharī parsed it as a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, being its qualifier, i.e. ما خلقت هذا خلقا باطلا (You did not create this in a vain creation) ... or it is by dropping the preposition, either the bāʾ or the lām.]»; (سبحان) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, its implied form being "نسبح" (we glorify), accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) a conjunction, linking cause and effect «[Note: It may be linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition.]»; (قنا) an imperative verb of supplication, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and (نا) a direct object, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anta"; (عذاب) a second direct object, accusative; (النار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «يذكرون ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يتفكّرون..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The vocative clause «ربنا ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied saying, and this saying is a ḥāl from the agent in (يذكرون and يتفكرون).
The clause «ما خلقت هذا باطلا» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «سبحانك» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «قنا عذاب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما خلقت «[Note: Or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if we fall short — or sin — then protect us from the punishment of the Fire.]».

* Morphology:
قياما is either the maṣdar of قام يقوم, of the pattern (bāb) نصر, its wazn being فعال with kasra on the fāʾ, or the plural of قائم, the active participle of قام يقوم, in which the wāw was converted to hamza because it comes after the alif of فاعل; its original is قاوم. In قيام there is a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion (qalb); its original is قواما, and it is a maṣdar or in the form of a maṣdar.
(قعودا) is either a hearsay-based (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb قعد يقعد, of the pattern نصر, its wazn being فعول with two ḍammas, or the plural of قاعد, the active participle of قعد, on the wazn فاعل.
(جنوب) plural of جنب, a noun for the side of a human or other; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): which gathers the three states of man in prayer, namely standing, sitting, and lying on the side or on the back.
2- Mursal (non-metaphorical) trope (al-majāz al-mursal): He mentioned «السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ», meaning the great bodies within them, of marvellous make, fit to be exploited for human benefit; the relation is that of place (maḥalliyya).
3- Concision (al-ījāz): in the saying of the Exalted «وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ».
For under this concision is folded all that science has brought forth of splendid discoveries and marvellous deductions.

* Benefits:
1- Faith between philosophy and the Qur'an.
You will hardly find anything greater or more comprehensive than these verses in the aspects of faith by way of reflection and the Qur'an. The philosophers almost agree that man has innate ideas, supplied by his intellect, for perceiving the truths that rational proofs and logical demonstrations cannot reach. Among these philosophers, the theists, are the early ones such as «Plato and Aristotle» of the Greek philosophers, and the later ones such as Descartes, Kant, Bergson and many others. All of them hold that man is able to rely on his innate ideas to perceive the existence of Allah; he need only look into the dominion of Allah and the perfection and originality that characterise Allah's creatures, from the atom to the galaxy, from the small plant to the great tree, from the grain of sand to the great mountain, and from the drop of water to the great ocean. All that points us, by an innate indication, to the existence of a great Originator behind this origination and invention. al-Ghazālī, al-Fārābī, Ibn Rushd and other philosophers and thinkers of Islam found no escape from resorting to this proof of His existence, the Exalted, alongside the complex and difficult scientific demonstrations. Perhaps all of them drew their guidance from the light of this verse, pausing long before «[Translator's note: the source reads «أما» (as for); «أمام» (before) appears to be meant.]» the saying of the Exalted:
«إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ لَآياتٍ لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ» to the end of the verses.

safi-cedvel:81-81.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر (remember); (أخذ) a past verb; (الله) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (ميثاق) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (النبيّين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ — and apparently it is with a muḍāf omitted — i.e. the followers of the prophets or the children of the prophets «[Note: This is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr, where he said: "So the beginning of the verse agrees with what follows it.. and what makes clear that the covenant was upon the nations is His saying فمن تولّى بعد ذلك فأولئك هم الفاسقون, and this supposition is impossible in the case of the prophets."]», (اللام) paving the way for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); (ما) a conditional noun making the verb jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi whose governor is آتيتكم «[Note: Ibn Kathīr said in his tafsīr: "i.e. whatever I give you of Book and wisdom, and then a messenger comes after it, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him." And (ما) may be a relative noun, mabnī, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its ṣila being the clause آتيتكم and the referent pronoun omitted, its implied form being آتيتكم إيّاه; and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is either His saying من كتاب وحكمة or the clause of an implied oath whose answer is لتؤمننّ به.. and the lām in this case is the lām of oath for an implied oath.. This is the choice of Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and others.]», (آتيت) a past verb, mabnī on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (التاء) is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (من كتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of (ما) or a tamyīz (specification) of it. (ثمّ) a conjunction; (جاء) a past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (رسول) fāʿil, nominative; (مصدّق) naʿt (adjective) of رسول, nominative like it; (اللام) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun, mabnī, in the position of genitive, attached to مصدّق; (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ṣila of ما, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (اللام) occurring in the answer to an oath; (تؤمننّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn — and it was deleted because of a succession of identical letters — and the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, and the nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis, with no grammatical position; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تؤمننّ); (الواو) conjunction; (لتنصرنّ) like لتؤمننّ.. and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is هو, i.e. Allah; (الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); (أقررتم) a past verb and its fāʿil; (الواو) conjunction; (أخذتم) like أقررتم; (على) a preposition and (ذا) a demonstrative, mabnī, in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the pronoun of address in His saying أخذتم; and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address, and (الميم) a particle for the masculine plural; (إصري) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa.. and the yāʾ is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قالوا) a past verb, mabnī on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أقررنا) like أقررتم; (قال) like the first; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition; (اشهدوا) an imperative verb, mabnī on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الواو) of the ḥāl; (أنا) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (معكم) like the first, attached to an omitted ḥāl of الشاهدين; (من الشاهدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of أنا.
The clause «أخذ الله..» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «آتيتكم..» has no grammatical position: explicative of the taking of the covenant.
The clause «جاءكم رسول» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause آتيتكم.
The clause «تؤمنن» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath. The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath «[Note: Abū Ḥayyān expressed some reservation about this i'rab, saying: "In it — i.e. in this assumed form — there is a very subtle flaw, because what is assumed must be of the same kind as what is overt, and the dependents of this one are the dependents of that one, and this does not hold with the clause جاءكم رسول conjoined to the clause آتيتكم, since it contains no pronoun referring back to the conditional noun.. So if the apodosis here is of a different kind from the answer to the oath, how can the answer to the oath indicate it.." (See al-Baḥr vol. 2 p. 511).]».
The clause «تنصرنّه» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause تؤمننّ.
The clause «قال..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أقررتم» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of the saying).
The clause «أخذتم» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause أقررتم.
The clause «قالوا..» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أقررنا» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «قال..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اشهدوا» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, joined with the fāʾ, i.e. إن أقررتم فاشهدوا (if you affirm, then bear witness). The implied condition together with its apodosis is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «أنا معكم من الشاهدين» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.. or resumptive with no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
1- «لَما آتَيْتُكُمْ»: the early scholars differed over the i'rab of «ما» in several ways, the most important being two. The first: the view of Sībawayh and al-Khalīl that «ما» means «الذي», the implied form of the speech being «الذي آتيتكموه»; the hāʾ, which is the referent pronoun, was deleted to lighten the pronunciation, and al-Akhfash held this view. On this view the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ) and «ما» is in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
The second: the view of al-Kisāʾī, al-Zajjāj and al-Mubarrad; their view is that «ما» is conditional and the lām is for verification, paving the way for the oath, because taking the covenant is equivalent to making someone swear, and the clause «تؤمننّ» is the answer to the oath, which makes the apodosis of the condition unnecessary.

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (من) a conditional noun making the verb jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (تولّى) a past verb, mabnī on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو; (بعد) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تولّى); (ذا) a demonstrative, mabnī, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (أولاء) a demonstrative, mabnī on the kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) «[Note: It may be parsed as a detached pronoun, a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is الفاسقون, and the nominal clause هم الفاسقون is the khabar of أولئك.]» to emphasize the quality of the khabar in الفاسقين; (الفاسقون) khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «من تولّى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تولّى بعد ذلك» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ من «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «أولئك..» الفاسقون is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
1- فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الْفاسِقُونَ: «هم» is a separating pronoun with no grammatical position; the separating pronoun, like «هو وأنا وأنت», stands between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar to signal that what follows it is a khabar and not a naʿt (adjective), and it gives the speech a kind of emphasis of the judgement, for added emphasis.

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of disapproval; (الفاء) conjunction or resumptive; (غير) a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (دين) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (يبغون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أسلم), which is a past verb; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil; (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila of من; (الواو) conjunction; (الأرض) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السموات, genitive like it; (طوعا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, accusative «[Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar because it is its synonym, for الطوع is synonymous with التسليم; or the verb أسلم has the meaning of "obeyed and submitted".]», (الواو) conjunction; (كرها) maʿṭūf to (طوعا), accusative like it; (الواو) conjunction; (إليه) like له, attached to (يرجعون), an imperfect verb, passive, nominative.. and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «يبغون» has no grammatical position: resumptive, or conjoined to an implied resumptive clause, the implied form being أيتولّون فغير دين الله يبغون ... (do they turn away, and seek other than the religion of Allah ...).
The clause «أسلم من في السموات» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «يرجعون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause أسلم.

* Morphology:
(يبغون): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making quiescent and by deletion; its original form is بيغيون: the ḍamma was found heavy on the yāʾ, so it was made quiescent and its vowel moved to the ghayn; then the yāʾ was deleted because it came quiescent before the quiescent wāw of the plural, so it became يبغون. «[Translator's note: The source writes «بيغيون»; the intended form is evidently يبغيون.]»
(طوعا): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb طاع يطوع, of the نصر class, and طاع يطاع, of the فتح class.. or it is a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the four-letter verb أطاع; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:84-84.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت; (آمنّا) a past verb and its fāʿil; (بالله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمنّا); (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, conjoined to the Name of Majesty; (أنزل) a past verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو; (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (أنزل); (الواو) conjunction; (ما) like the first and conjoined to it; (أنزل على) like the first; (إبراهيم) a genitive noun, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, attached to (أنزل); (إسماعيل، إسحاق، يعقوب، الأسباط) nouns conjoined to إبراهيم by conjunctions, genitive like it; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a noun like the first and conjoined to it; (أوتي) like أنزل; (موسى) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (عيسى، النبيّون) two nouns conjoined to موسى, nominative like it, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma and the wāw respectively; (من ربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied pronoun in (أوتي), i.e. ما أوتيه موسى ... منزلا من ربّهم (what Mūsā ... was given, sent down from their Lord) «[Note: Or attached to (أوتي).]», and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (لا) negating; (نفرّق) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being نحن; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (نفرّق); (أحد) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أحد; (الواو) conjunction; (نحن) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (مسلمون), which is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «قل..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنّا بالله» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl (the object of the saying).
The clause «أنزل علينا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (ما).
The clause «أنزل على إبراهيم» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (ما).
The clause «أوتي موسى» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative (ما).
The clause «لا نفرّق» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «نحن له مسلمون» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the ḥāl clause.

* Morphology:
(الأسباط): plural of سبط, a noun for the daughter's son in his relation to his grandfather; but it is used in the verse in the sense of grandchildren, because they are the children of Yaʿqūb, so they are the grandchildren of Ibrāhīm.. The pattern of سبط is فعل with kasra then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(كدأب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "their custom" (دأبهم) «[Note: Or attached to an implied maṣdar, and there are several views on its implied form: first: they disbelieved with a disbelief like the habit of the people of Pharaoh; second: they were punished with a punishment like the custom of the people of Pharaoh; third: their benefit from wealth and children came to nothing, like the habit of the people of Pharaoh; fourth: they denied with a denial like the custom of the people of Pharaoh (Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī mentioned that).]»; (آل) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (فرعون) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote because of being a proper name and foreign; (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, maʿṭūf (conjoined) to آل فرعون «[Note: Or in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause كذّبوا بآياتنا, and the clause has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause (دأبهم ...).]»; (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (كذّبوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (بآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (كذّبوا), and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunction, carrying the meaning of causation; (أخذ) a past verb, and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (بذنوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخذ), which has been made to include the meaning of "destroyed", and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (شديد) khabar, nominative; (العقاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «(دأبهم) كدأب آل فرعون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كذّبوا» has no grammatical position; it is explicative of the resumptive clause «[Note: Or it is an explanatory resumption; or it is the khabar if the relative noun (الذين) is parsed as a mubtadaʾ, with the speech being complete at His words آل فرعون; or it is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), with an implied قد, i.e. "denying".]».
The clause «أخذهم الله» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause كذّبوا.
The clause «لله شديد العقاب» [Translator's note: so in the source, for الله شديد العقاب] has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(دأب): maṣdar of دأب يدأب, of the فتح pattern; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(ذنوب): plural of ذنب, a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the quadriliteral أذنب; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representative simile (tashbīh tamthīlī): in His words, the Exalted: «إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً، وَأُولئِكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ، كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ».
The ayah contains the likening of the state of the polytheists — in their striving in their disbelief, their banding together against the Prophet, upon him be peace, and their denial of the signs of Allah that he brought — to the state of the people of Pharaoh in their banding together against Moses, upon him be peace, and their denial of the signs of Allah that he brought. The point of resemblance is composed of a number of things taken together: immersion in disbelief, their enmity toward the Prophet, and denial of the signs of Allah, and not of any single one of these things. So the simile is representative (tamthīlī).

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the agent is "anta" (you); (اللام) a preposition; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قل); (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (السين) a particle of the future; (تغلبون) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (الواو) conjunction; (تحشرون) like تغلبون; (إلى جهنّم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb تحشرون, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, for it is a diptote because of being a proper name and feminine; (الواو) resumptive; (بئس) a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; (المهاد) fāʿil, nominative; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. Jahannam.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ستغلبون» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «تحشرون» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the speech reported.
The clause «بئس المهاد» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive «[Note: Or in the position of a nominative as khabar (predicate) of the omitted one specified for blame, and the nominal clause is resumptive.]».

* Benefits:
1- بئس المهاد:
«ما» may be joined to نعم, as in نعمّا يعظكم به, and it is of three kinds:
a- Single, not followed by anything, as in: دققته دقّا نعمّا ("I pounded it a pounding, how excellent!"); it is a complete definite (maʿrifa tāmma), the agent, and the one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. "excellent is the thing, the pounding".
b- That it be followed by a single word, as in «فنعمّا هي»; in this case it is parsed as the agent, and what follows it is the one specified.
c- That it be followed by a verbal clause, as in «نعمّا يعظكم به» and «بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم»; then «ما» is parsed as an indefinite in the position of an accusative as tamyīz (specification), and the one specified is omitted, i.e. "excellent as a thing with which He admonishes you is that saying".

safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (كان) a defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters); (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of كان; (آية) the postponed noun of كان, nominative; (في فئتين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آية, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is a dual; (التقت) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; and (التاء) is the tāʾ of the feminine, and (الألف) an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as fāʿil (agent); (فئة) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "one of them" (إحداهما) «[Note: It is permissible for it to be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause تقاتل; beginning with an indefinite is permitted because it is in a context of detailing.]»; (تقاتل) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هي"; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقاتل); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (أخرى) mubtadaʾ, nominative «[Note: It is permissible for it to be conjoined to the word فئة, so there is no need to imply a khabar, but rather to imply a naʿt.]», the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the alif; (كافرة) naʿt of أخرى, nominative like it; and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "fights in the way of the ṭāghūt"; (يرون) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (مثلي) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (رأي) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative; (العين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
(الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (يؤيّد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (بنصر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤيّد), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (يشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (في) a preposition; (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to the omitted fronted khabar of (إنّ); (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) a particle of address; (اللام) the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), giving emphasis; (عبرة) the postponed noun of إنّ, accusative; (لأولي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of عبرة, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (الأبصار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «قد كان لكم ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «التقتا» is in the position of a genitive as naʿt of فئتين.
The clause «تقاتل» is in the position of a nominative as naʿt of فئة «[Note: It is permissible for it to be a khabar if (فئة) is parsed as a mubtadaʾ.]».
The clause «يرونهم ...» is in the position of a nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ أخرى «[Note: It is permissible for the clause to be in the position of a nominative as naʿt of أخرى.]».
The clause «الله يؤيّد ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يؤيّد بنصره» is in the position of a nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «يشاء» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إنّ في ذلك لعبرة» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(التقتا): it contains iʿlāl by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescent letters: the alif — the lām of the word — was deleted because it came quiescent before the tāʾ of the feminine; its wazn is افتعتا.
(رأي): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb رأى; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(نصر): an aurally-transmitted maṣdar of the verb نصر; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn (see ayah 214 of Sūrat al-Baqara).
(يشاء): iʿlāl by substitution (qalb); its original form is يشيأ, with a yāʾ bearing fatḥa; then its vowel was moved to the shīn and it was made quiescent; then the yāʾ was changed to an alif because it was originally voweled and the letter before it has a fatḥa. (See ayah 247 of Sūrat al-Baqara).
(عبرة): a maṣdar of عبر يعبر, of the فتح pattern, or a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the five-letter verb اعتبر; its wazn is فعلة, with kasra on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Iḥtibāk: it is omission from two corresponding statements, each of which indicates what is omitted from the other. This is in His words: «فِئَةٌ تُقاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَأُخْرى كافِرَةٌ»: each of them is a mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, i.e. a believing party fights [Translator's note: the source has تقابل, "faces", evidently a misprint for تقاتل] in the way of Allah, and another, disbelieving party fights in the way of Satan.
2- Double-directed speech (al-kalām al-muwajjah): because a meaning is either understood as one single thing admitting nothing else, or it admits the thing and something other; and that otherness is either an opposite or not. This ayah admits two different meanings, and that otherness is an opposite, since the seeing of the multitude may be attributed to the Muslims or to the polytheists at one and the same time, and there is nothing that gives preference to one over the other, because each of them can validly be applied in the ayah.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(زيّن) a passive past verb; (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (زيّن); (حبّ) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (الشهوات) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (من النساء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الشهوات; (البنين، القناطير) two nouns conjoined to النساء by the two conjunctions, the sign of the genitive in البنين being the yāʾ, for it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (المقنطرة) naʿt (adjective) of القناطير, genitive like it; (من الذهب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of القناطير or of المقنطرة; (الواو) conjunction; (الفضّة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الذهب, genitive like it; (الخيل، الأنعام، الحرث) nouns conjoined to النساء by conjunctions, genitive; (المسوّمة) naʿt of الخيل, genitive like it. (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) for distance, and (الكاف) for address; (متاع) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الحياة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الدنيا) naʿt of الحياة, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (عند) an adverb of place — or of time —, accusative, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (حسن) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (المآب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «زيّن للناس حبّ ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «ذلك متاع» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «الله عنده حسن ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «عنده حسن المآب» is in the position of a nominative as khabar.

* Morphology:
(حبّ): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb حب يحب, of the ضرب pattern; its wazn is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn (see 165 of Sūrat al-Baqara).
(الشهوات): plural of شهوة, which is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the verb اشتهى; its wazn is فعلة, with fatḥa then sukūn; or it is an aurally-transmitted maṣdar of the verb شها يشهو or شهي يشهي, of the فرح pattern.
(البنين): a plural treated like the sound plural, because its singular is ابن, the form of the singular having changed in the plural; but it was treated as the sound plural: nominative with the wāw, and accusative and genitive with the yāʾ. The alif in ابن is additional, and it is a compensation for the deleted lām of the word, which is the wāw; its wazn is افع.
(القناطير): plural of القنطار. It is said that the nūn in it is radical, so its wazn is فعلال, with kasra on the fāʾ; and it is said that it is additional, because it is from قطر يقطر, of the نصر pattern, when it flows: silver and gold are likened to water in abundance and quickness of turnover; on this view its wazn is فنعال. There has been disagreement over the weight of the qinṭār in ancient and modern times, but most commonly it is a hundred raṭl.
(المقنطرة): passive participle of the quadriliteral قنطر; its wazn is مفعللة, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the two lāms.
(الخيل): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) having no singular from its own root; its singular is فرس. It is also said that its singular is خائل, and it is derived from الخيلاء (pride), like طير and طائر.
(المسوّمة): passive participle of the quadriliteral سوّم, and the tāʾ is for the feminine suited to the plural; its wazn is مفعّلة, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the doubled ʿayn.
(الأنعام): plural of نعم — with fatḥa on the nūn and the ʿayn —; النعم is a collective noun having no singular from its own root; it is treated as masculine and feminine and applies to camels, cattle and sheep, and the plural is أنعام in consideration of its three kinds.
(حسن): an aurally-transmitted maṣdar of the verb حسن يحسن, of the نصر pattern and the كرم pattern; its wazn is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn (ayah 83, al-Baqara).
(المآب): its wazn is مفعل, with fatḥa on the ʿayn; its original form is مأوب, because it is from آب يئوب; then the vowel of the wāw, which is the fatḥa, was moved to the hamza, and it was made quiescent, and the wāw was changed to an alif because it was originally voweled and the letter before it has a fatḥa, so it became مآبا. It is a mīmī maṣdar meaning "return", and it may be a noun of place or a noun of time of the verb آب.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the ayah there is the device of murāʿāt al-naẓīr (congruity), which is that the poet or prose writer brings together a thing and what suits it, while dispensing with mention of contrast, so that it falls outside muqābala (contrast) and muṭābaqa (antithesis). In this ayah He, Glorified is He, has brought together most of the means of enjoyment that lead a person to become absorbed in temptation and to be led along by the urges of unruly souls; they have been made attractive to people and have enticed them with wonders and charms.

* Benefits:
1- Murāʿāt al-naẓīr: that is by enumerating the blessings of this world that man desires. It is counted among the semantic embellishments (al-muḥassināt al-maʿnawiyya) to which the souls of poets were drawn for a period of time. Folk poets still excel at this art and its like, and take it as a means of competing with their peers among poets.
2- القناطير «المقنطرة»: what is meant by the word «المقنطرة» is emphasis, as in their saying «ألف مؤلفة، وبدرة مبدرة» ("a thousand made into thousands, a purse made into purses"). And المسوّمة means «المعلّمة» (marked), from أسامها الله وسوّمها in the sense of "He pastured them".

safi-cedvel:124-124.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نصركم) in the previous verse [Note: It may be a badal (substitute) of His saying إِذْ هَمَّتْ in verse (122), because the story in both is one on this view ... There is great disagreement among the exegetes in the interpretation of this verse; I quote a summary of it from al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ of Abū Ḥayyān. He said: The apparent sense of this verse is its connection with what precedes it, because it is part of the story of Badr, and this is the view of the majority; so (إذ) is governed by (نصركم). It was also said that this belongs to the completion of the story of Uḥud, so His saying ولقد نصركم الله ببدر is parenthetical between the two passages, because of the urging to reliance on Allah and steadfastness in fighting that it contains. The argument for this view is that on the day of Badr the reinforcement of angels was a thousand, while here it is three thousand and five thousand ... And He said:
يأتوكم من فورهم, i.e. the reinforcement - meaning the reinforcement of the disbelievers - whereas on the day of Badr the Muslims went to them.], (تقول) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنت. (للمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقول), and the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ. (الهمزة) for interrogation of denial (istifhām inkārī). (لن) a particle of negation and of the accusative. (يكفي) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle and of the accusative. (يمدّ) an imperfect verb, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (ربّ) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يمدّكم ربّكم) is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil of يكفي.
(بثلاثة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يمدّكم), (آلاف) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) [Note: It is well known that the tamyīz (specification) of a hundred and a thousand and their multiples is a singular in the genitive by annexation; so the numeral word is not given tanwīn except when the muḍāf ilayhi is deleted, as in this verse. The implied tamyīz in this verse is: ثلاثة آلاف ملك من الملائكة (three thousand angels from among the angels).], (من الملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the implied tamyīz, which is ملك. (منزلين) ḥāl (circumstantial) of الملائكة, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ [Note: i.e. Allah reinforces you with help in the state of the angels' descending to the earth ...].
The clause «تقول ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لن يكفيكم ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يمدّكم ربّكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(منزلين), plural of منزل - with fatḥa on the zāy - a passive participle from the quadriliteral أنزل; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn. In the word the hamza was deleted from its beginning, just as it was deleted from the verb.

* Benefits:
- His saying, the Exalted: «أَلَنْ يَكْفِيَكُمْ»: the hamza is for interrogation of disapproval (istinkārī), and it has turned the negation into an affirmation. We have already seen that the hamza departs from its original meaning for which it was coined, which is interrogation. To fix that in the minds of readers, we return to establish it in detail. It occurs for eight meanings:
1- The hamza of equalisation (taswiya): it is the one that comes after the word سواء or what has its meaning, and is followed by a clause in whose place a maṣdar may properly stand, as in: «سَواءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ» 2- Invalidating denial (al-inkār al-ibṭālī): it requires that what follows it - if the interrogation is removed - did not occur, as in His saying, the Exalted: أَفَأَصْفاكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِالْبَنِينَ وَاتَّخَذَ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ إِناثاً.
3- Reproachful denial (al-inkār al-tawbīkhī): it is the one where what follows it did occur and its doer is blameworthy, as in: «أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ».
4- Affirmation (taqrīr): it is your leading the addressee to acknowledge and confess a matter whose affirmation or negation is settled with him.
5- Mockery (tahakkum), as in «قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا» 6- Command, as in: «أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ», i.e. submit (أسلموا).
7- Wonder (taʿajjub), as in: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ؟ 8- Finding slow (istibṭāʾ), as in: أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ؟!

safi-cedvel:125-125.t:
* I'rab:
(بلى) a particle of answer, affirming the negated question: ألن يكفيكم.. (إن) a jussive-causing conditional particle. (تصبروا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الواو) conjunction. (تتّقوا) like تصبروا and conjoined to it. (الواو) conjunction. (يأتوا) like تصبروا and conjoined to it, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (من فور) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتوا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh). (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive as naʿt (adjective) of فور or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of it. (يمدد) an imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (ربّ) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi. (بخمسة آلاف من الملائكة) like its counterpart in the previous verse. (مسوّمين) ḥāl (circumstantial) of الملائكة, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «إن تصبروا..» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «تتقوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تصبروا.
The clause «يأتوكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تصبروا.
The clause «يمددكم ربّكم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(الفور), an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb فار يفور, of the class of نصر, meaning to hasten and hurry; from it comes فارت القدر, i.e. the pot's boiling intensified and its contents rushed to come out.. Or it is a noun meaning the immediate moment or the state in which there is no delay. Its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مسوّمين), plural of مسوّم - with kasra on the wāw - an active participle from the quadriliteral سوّم with doubled ʿayn; its pattern is مفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the doubled ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- بلى is a particle of answer like نعم. The particles of answer are:
«لا، نعم، بلى، إي، أجل، جلل، جير، إنّ».
Each of these particles has characteristics that we can address individually whenever the time comes for one of them.

safi-cedvel:126-126.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction. (ما) negative. (جعل) a past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is the reinforcement. (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (إلا) a particle of restriction. (بشرى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif [Note: or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) if (جعل) is transitive to one object.], (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of بشرى. (الواو) conjunction. (اللام) causal (li-l-taʿlīl). (تطمئن) an imperfect verb, accusative by (أن) concealed after the lām. (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of القلوب [Note: or attached to (تطمئنّ).].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تطمئنّ قلوبكم) is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, attached to an omitted verb indicated by the mentioned verb جعل; or it is conjoined to بشرى and was put in the genitive with the lām because a condition of the accusative was lacking.
(الواو) resumptive. (ما) negative. (النصر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative. (إلّا) a particle of restriction. (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (العزيز) naʿt of الله, genitive like it, and likewise الحكيم.
The clause «ما جعله الله ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous verse.
The clause «تطمئنّ قلوبكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «the implied جعل» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the overt clause جعله.
The clause «ما النّصر إلّا» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

safi-cedvel:127-127.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) causal (li-l-taʿlīl). (يقطع) an imperfect verb, accusative by (إن) [Translator's note: thus in the source; the particle meant is أن] concealed after the lām, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو, i.e. Allah. (طرفا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من) a preposition. (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (طرفا), (كفروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقطع) is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, attached to the "being" (al-istiqrār) to which (من عند) in the previous verse is attached, i.e. victory is from Allah in order to cut off a portion of those who disbelieved [Note: It may be attached to the maṣdar (النصر) in the previous verse, or to an implied verb, i.e. نصركم ليقطع (He gave you victory to cut off) or أمدّكم (He reinforced you), or to the verb نصركم mentioned in verse (123), what lies between them being parenthetical.].
(أو) a conjunction. (يكبت) like يقطع and conjoined to it, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being هو. (الفاء) conjunction. (ينقلبوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يكبتهم), and the sign of the accusative is the deletion of the nūn..
and the wāw is the fāʿil. (خائبين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «يقطع ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يكبتهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقطع; and the clause «ينقلبوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يكبتهم.

* Morphology:
(طرفا), a noun meaning a group or portion; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(خائبين), plural of خائب, an active participle from خاب يخيب, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is فاعل, and in it the weak letter is regularly converted into a hamza after the alif of فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
«لِيَقْطَعَ طَرَفاً مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا» i.e. to destroy a group of them by killing and capture. He likened those of them who were killed and scattered to a thing cut off whose parts have been scattered and whose order has been disrupted. This is of the type of the explicit, dependent metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya).

safi-cedvel:128-128.t:
* I'rab:
(ليس) an inflexible (jāmid) defective past verb. (اللام) a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of the defective verb. (من الأمر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of شيء - a naʿt (adjective) placed before what it qualifies -. (شيء) the postponed ism (subject) of ليس, nominative (marfūʿ). (أو) a conjunction meaning إلى (until). (يتوب) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by (أن) concealed after أو, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هو. (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (يتوب), (أو) conjunction. (يعذّب) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يتوب), and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "He". (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya). (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the ism of إنّ. (ظالمون) khabar, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتوب ...) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to شيء; the implied form is: ليس شيء من أجلهم منك أو توبة عليهم من الله (nothing on their account is from you, or [it is] a turning in forgiveness to them from Allah).
The clause «ليس لك من الأمر شيء» has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يتوب ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «يعذّبهم» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يتوب.
The clause «إنّهم ظالمون» has no grammatical position, causal.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, the Exalted: «أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ» is accusative by أن optionally concealed after «أو». Among the particles that put the imperfect verb in the accusative, «أن» is distinguished by governing the accusative both overt and concealed, and its governing while concealed is of two kinds: «optional and obligatory». The optional is in six places, or after six particles: the first is the lām of kay, which is the causal lām; the second is the lām of consequence (lām al-ʿāqiba), what follows which is a result of what precedes it, also called the lām of becoming (al-ṣayrūra) and the lām of outcome (al-natīja); the third, fourth, fifth and sixth are «the conjunctions الواو، الفاء، ثمّ and أو». The condition for its being in the accusative after them by concealed أن is that it is necessarily conjoined to a pure noun, i.e. a primitive (jāmid) non-derived noun. As for its being obligatorily concealed, that is after five particles:
The first: the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), which some called the lām of negation. The second: the fāʾ of causation. The third: the wāw of accompaniment (al-maʿiyya). The fourth: حتى the preposition which means إلى or the causal lām. The fifth: أو in whose place «إلى or إلّا» may properly stand, as in the saying of the poet:
لاستسهلنّ الصعب أو أدرك المنى ... فما انقادت الآمال إلا لصابر.
(I will surely make the difficult easy until I attain my hopes ... for hopes have yielded only to one who is patient.)

I would have liked to cite evidence for each of the places of the optional and the obligatory, were it not that this might take us out of the aim and moderation in what we are engaged in.

safi-cedvel:192-192.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا) its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse, and it is an emphasis of the preceding vocative; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of (إن); (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, a fronted first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (تدخل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the sukūn, vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, its fāʿil (agent) a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anta"; (النار) a second direct object, accusative (manṣūb); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq); (أخزيت) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (التاء) is the agent, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object; (الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative; (للظالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (من) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (أنصار) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
The clause «ربّنا إنك ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, seeking mercy — or resumptive.
The clause «إنّك من تدخل ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «ندخل النار» «[Translator's note: so in the source; «تدخل النار» is meant.]» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar of inna.
The clause «قد أخزيته» is in the position of a jussive: the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما للظالمين من أنصار» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
1- Making the Fire explicit in the place of a pronoun: to magnify its terror; and mentioning "causing to enter" in the context of punishment, to specify its manner and show the extreme of its horror.
2- In the verse is the device of prolixity (al-iṭnāb): which is the excess of wording over meaning for a benefit, in several ways, among them:
a- Mentioning the specific after the general: to draw attention to the merit of the specific.
b- Mentioning the general after the specific: its purpose is to convey comprehensiveness while giving attention to the specific.
c- Clarification after vagueness.
d- Repetition (al-takrīr): «ربّنا» is mentioned repeatedly, for humble entreaty, to show complete submission, and to present the acknowledgement of His Lordship, the Exalted, together with faith in Him.
e- Parenthesis (al-iʿtirāḍ): which is to bring, in the midst of speech or between two pieces of speech connected in meaning, a clause with no grammatical position for a secondary benefit.
And precaution (al-iḥtirās): which is every addition that comes to ward off something the speech might suggest that is not intended.
3- «وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصارٍ»: in the verse is the device of putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun. He put «the wrongdoers» in the place of the pronoun referring to those made to enter, to blame them and to indicate that the cause of their entering the Fire is their wrongdoing and their putting things in other than their proper places.

safi-cedvel:193-193.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا) its i'rab has passed «[Note: in verse (191) of this sūra.]»; (إننا) like إنك in the previous verse; (سمعنا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.. and (نا) is the fāʿil (agent); (مناديا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (ينادي) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "huwa"; (للإيمان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينادي) «[Note: The lām is in the sense of إلى (to); it is said to be causal.. and it is said to be in the sense of the bāʾ.]»; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle «[Note: And the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive governed by an omitted preposition, namely the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun «[Translator's note: the footnote breaks off here in the source.]»]»; (آمنوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the agent; (بربّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (آمنوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الفاء) a conjunction, linking the effect to the cause; (آمنّا) like سمعنا; (ربّنا) its i'rab has passed; (الفاء) a conjunction linking the effect to the cause; (اغفر) an imperative verb of supplication, its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "anta"; (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (اغفر); (ذنوب) a direct object, accusative, and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (كفّر عنّا سيّئاتنا) like اغفر لنا ذنوبنا, the preposition being attached to (كفّر), and the sign of the accusative in the object being the kasra; (الواو) a conjunction; (توفّ) an imperative of supplication, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and (نا) a pronoun, direct object, and the agent is "anta"; (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (توفّنا); (الأبرار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «ربّنا إننا ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption repeated to seek mercy.
The clause «إننا سمعنا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the vocative.
The clause «سمعنا مناديا» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna.
The clause «ينادي ...» is in the position of an accusative: naʿt (adjective) of (مناديا) «[Note: attached to (ينادي). (أن) may be a particle of explanation (tafsīr), and the clause after it has no grammatical position: explicative.]».
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «آمنّا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنوا.
The clause «ربّنا (the second)» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, seeking mercy.
The clause «اغفر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آمنا «[Note: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī made it a second direct object of the verb سمعنا.
It may be the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e.: if You accept our faith, then forgive ...]».
The clause «كفّر ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اغفر.
The clause «توفّنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اغفر.

* Morphology:
(مناديا) active participle from the quadriliteral نادى; its wazn is مفاعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(توفّنا) it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion suited to the indeclinable form: in its imperfect it was يتوفّاه الله (Allah takes him [in death]), and the weak letter was deleted in the imperative; its wazn is تفعنا.
(الأبرار) plural of برّ, from the verb برّ يبرّ, of the patterns (bāb) نصر and ضرب; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, and it is an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) ... As for بارّ, the active participle of برّ, its plural is بررة, whose wazn is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām.

safi-cedvel:194-194.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا) its i'rab has passed «[Note: in verse (191) of this sūra.]»; (الواو) a conjunction; (آتنا) like قنا in the previous verse «[Translator's note: قنا occurs in verse 191, not 193.]»; (ما) a relative noun «[Note: It may be a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of an accusative, a direct object, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e.: the outcome of Your promise.]», indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (وعدت) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and (التاء) is the fāʿil (agent), and (نا) a pronoun, direct object; (على رسل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وعدتنا), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. on the tongues of Your messengers, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) the prohibitive lā, jussive-governing; (تخز) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, its agent a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "anta", and (نا) a pronoun, direct object; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (تخزنا); (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of inna; (لا) negative; (تخلف) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its agent a latent pronoun, implied as "anta"; (الميعاد) a direct object, accusative.
The clause «ربّنا» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «آتنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause توفّنا in the previous verse.
The clause «وعدتنا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the nominal or particle relative (ما).
The clause «لا تخزنا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتنا..
The clause «إنّك لا تخلف ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya) ...
The clause «لا تخلف ...» is in the position of a nominative: the khabar (predicate) of inna..

* Rhetoric:
1- In this noble verse is the device of «al-isjāl» (affirmation by record), an unparalleled device. Its definition is that the speaker intends some purpose and brings words that establish that purpose:
The Master, Glorified and Exalted, has recorded, on the tongues of His servants, the fulfilment of what He promised on the tongue of His Messenger, and that is in His saying «ما وَعَدْتَنا»; you find that this promise has become binding, its binding never to be undone.

safi-cedvel:164-164.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (منّ) a past verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (على المؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (منّ), the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ; (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (منّ); (بعث) a past verb, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (في) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (بعث); (رسولا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (من أنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (رسولا), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (يتلو) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the wāw, and its fāʿil is "he"; (عليهم) like فيهم, attached to (يتلو); (آيات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the kasra, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (يزكّي) like يتلو, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (يعلّمهم) like يزكيهم; (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (الحكمة) conjoined to الكتاب, accusative like it; (الواو) of the ḥāl (circumstantial); (إن) lightened from the heavy (inna), inoperative; (كانوا) a deficient past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the noun of kāna; (من) a preposition; (قبل) a noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to the notion of "being settled" (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar (predicate) is attached; (اللام) is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), which signals that (إن) is lightened; (في ضلال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of كانوا; (مبين) a naʿt of ضلال, genitive like it.
The clause «منّ الله» has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «بعث ...» is in the position of genitive, (إذ) being annexed to it.
The clause «يتلو ...» is in the position of accusative, either as a ḥāl of (رسولا) or as a naʿt of it.
The clause «يزكّيهم» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «يعلّمهم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the accusative pronoun in يعلّمهم.

* Morphology:
(ضلال): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb ضلّ يضلّ, of the ḍaraba class (bāb ḍaraba); its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this noble verse there is an art among the arts of rhetoric known as the art of tajrīd (abstraction): the speaker extracts from something possessing a quality another thing like it in that quality, to intensify the perfection of that quality in it, as though it were more eloquent than simply describing it by that quality. Here it is in His saying «من», the preposition.

* Benefits:
1- In this verse there are two benefits worth pointing out:
First: «وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ لَفِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ»: this lām in the word «لفي» is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); its origin is the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and it is called "distinguishing" only because it distinguishes between «إن» lightened from the heavy and the negative إن, as in «وَإِنْ كُلٌّ لَمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ». When «إن» enters upon a verb it is necessarily inoperative. Most commonly the verb is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: وَإِنْ كانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ. It may be an abrogating imperfect verb, as in «إِنْ يَكادُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَيُزْلِقُونَكَ». Less common than that is for it to be a non-abrogating past verb, and less common still for it to be a non-abrogating imperfect verb, which by consensus is not taken as a basis for analogy, as in «إن يرينك لنفسك».
Second: in the verse there is the art of tajrīd, which is that the speaker extracts from himself another who represents him in ability or otherwise, as in the saying of Shawqī:
قم ناج جلّق وأنشد رسم من بانوا ... مشت على الرسم أحداث وأزمان
(Rise, speak intimately to Jilliq [Damascus] and recite to the traces of those who have departed; events and ages have trodden upon the traces.)
Poets frequently resort to it at the openings of odes.

safi-cedvel:165-165.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (al-istifhām al-inkārī); (الواو) resumptive; (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when" (حين), containing the sense of condition, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis قلتم; (أصابت) a past verb.. and (التاء) is for the feminine, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (مصيبة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (أصبتم) a past verb and its fāʿil; (مثلي) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (قلتم) like أصبتم; (أنّى) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate), the meaning being (from where is this?); (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (قل) an imperative verb, its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "you" (أنت); (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (أنفس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (انّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (على كلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدير; (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (قدير) the khabar of inna, nominative.
The clause «أصابتكم مصيبة.» is in the position of genitive, (لمّا) being annexed to it.
The clause «قد أصبتم.» is in the position of nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of مصيبة.
The clause «قلتم.» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivizing condition.
The clause «أنّى هذا» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb "to say" (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قل» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هو من عند ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «إنّ الله.. قدير..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Benefits:
1- «أو لمّا»: in this word three words have come together: the hamza of interrogation, the wāw of conjunction, and لمّا meaning "when". What concerns us in explaining this benefit is «لمّا», for it has three technical uses:
The first: that it is jussivizing; it is specific to entering upon the imperfect verb and puts it in the jussive. It is one of the four jussivizing particles that put a single imperfect verb in the jussive, namely «لم، لما، the lām of command and the prohibitive لا». Like «لم», it has the special property of converting the time of the imperfect into the past.
The second: it is specific to the past verb. The grammarians have two views about it: some say that it is an adverb meaning «حين» ("when"), and others hold that it is a particle linking two clauses, as in «لمّا جاءني أكرمته» ("When he came to me, I honoured him"). The third: that it is a particle of exception, as in «إِنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمَّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ»; this is specific to entering upon the nominal clause.

safi-cedvel:166-166.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (أصاب) a past verb, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "it" (هو), and it is the resumptive pronoun (al-ʿāʾid); (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أصاب); (التقى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الجمعان) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the alif; (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate), because the mubtadaʾ resembles a condition; (بإذن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ whose implied form is "it" (هو) «[Note: This is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān.. and it is permissible for the preposition to be attached to the khabar of ما, i.e. what befell you ...
occurred by Allah's permission.]»; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of causation (taʿlīl); (يعلم) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām, its fāʿil a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو), i.e. Allah; (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يعلم..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to what بإذن الله is attached to, because it is conjoined to it «[Note: It is permissible to attach it to an omitted verb, i.e. He did that as a test and so that He might know the believers.]».
The clause «ما أصابكم ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أصابكم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «(هو) بإذن الله» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
The clause «يعلم..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the maṣdar relative particle (أن).
The clause «التقى الجمعان» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

* Benefits:
1- «فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ»: this fāʾ suggests that it links an apodosis, and an objector might object to that by saying: there is no apodosis except for a condition, and there is no condition in this verse. But we answer this objection by saying that, in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَما أَصابَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعانِ», «ما», even though it is closer to being a relative, is imbued with the spirit of condition and resembles it; therefore it was acceptable for the fāʾ to come in its answer, and thus it is established that the fāʾ links the answer.
2- The saying of Allah the Exalted: «يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْواهِهِمْ ما لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ» is decisive proof that speech is of two kinds, the speech of the tongue and the speech of the heart, and that the hypocrite always and forever shows what he does not conceal «[Translator's note: so in the source (يبدي ما لا يخفي); presumably "shows what he does not hold inwardly" is meant.]», and says words with his tongue while knowing the falsity and slander of those words and that they are entirely different from what he harbours in his heart; had he believed, he would have known that Allah knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal. «[Translator's note: this verse is part of the following verse (3:167).]»

safi-cedvel:167-167.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (ليعلم) like the one in the previous verse.
The interpreted maṣdar is genitive by the lām and attached to (mutaʿalliq) what the previous interpreted maṣdar is attached to, because it is conjoined to it.
(الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (نافقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (الواو) conjunction - or resumptive -; (قيل) a past verb in the passive; (اللام) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (قيل); (تعالوا) an inert (jāmid) imperative verb ... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (قاتلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قاتلوا) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of قاتلوا, i.e. fight, proceeding in the way of Allah.]»; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أو) a conjunction; (ادفعوا) like قاتلوا; (قالوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (لو) a non-jussivizing conditional particle; (نعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "we" (نحن); (قتالا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لو; (اتّبعنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn..
